text:
Wyatt Johnston spent the first month of the season getting chances and not cashing them, and that has started to change. He scored in four straight games through Nov. 19, one of them a late goal at Vegas that The Athletic's Jesse Granger described as a "Fortunate bounce for the Stars," and he's on a five-game point streak. Last season's 45-goal scorer now has 7 goals and 21 points in 21 games, 11 of those points on the power play.

The goals are still the part that lags. He has built 11.2 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and turned them into 7. That gap usually closes for a player who keeps getting to the net, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 93rd percentile for chances from the slot last season. Our numbers project about 31 goals and 78 points. The thing to watch is at the other end: Evolving-Hockey found opponents got more chances with him on the ice last season, and this year Dallas is roughly even in expected goals with him at five on five.
headline: Wyatt Johnston's goals are catching up to his chances
